provenance.generatedBy: claude-opus-5-5 · Field Kit v2 Prompt A batch
provenance.notes: Int family batch. Design-led, portfolio sells; copy leans on the design consult, closet types, garage systems and finishes. No closet-system, hardware or franchise brands. Ranges are planning figures, not quotes.

pageStructurePlus.contains: The in-home measure, a rendered closet design with elevations, finish and hardware samples, a revision round, and how the design becomes the order
pageStructurePlus.why: Buyers can't picture a custom closet from a bare wall. The design consultation is the product, and showing it is what books the measure.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Walk-in and reach-in closets, pantries, laundry rooms, mudroom lockers, kids' closets that grow, and home office wall systems, each with a sample layout
pageStructurePlus.why: People shop by room. A page per closet type catches the search and shows them a layout close to their own.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Slatwall panels, overhead ceiling racks, garage cabinets and workbenches, bike and sports gear storage, weight ratings and keeping room for the cars
pageStructurePlus.why: Garage buyers decide on capacity and cleanliness. Showing weight ratings and finished garages wins the bigger job.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Melamine colours and wood-grain finishes, drawer fronts, soft-close drawers, LED closet lighting, jewellery and valet inserts, tie and belt racks, mirrors and islands
pageStructurePlus.why: Accessories are where the ticket grows. Buyers only add them when they see them laid out on a finished closet.

pageStructurePlus.section: Install day: empty, remove and install
pageStructurePlus.contains: What to empty beforehand, removing old wire shelving, patching and painting the walls, how long a walk-in or a garage takes, and haul-away
pageStructurePlus.why: The fear of emptying a closet holds people back. A clear install-day page turns it into a weekend plan.

designDirections.name: Everything in Its Place
designDirections.bestFor: Small closet and garage installers who win on a fast free measure and clear package prices
designDirections.headlineSample: Custom closets and garage storage in {City}
designDirections.whyItFits: Riso blue and geometric caps feel crisp and organised, like labelled bins, and the page drives to the free-measure form.

designDirections.name: Walk-In Gallery
designDirections.bestFor: Closet designers with a strong portfolio of walk-ins, pantries and garages to sort by room
designDirections.headlineSample: Closets and garages designed around your things in {City}
designDirections.whyItFits: The family combo, Terracotta Kiln, fails the CTA contrast rule. Driftwood keeps the refined serif and warm neutrals with a walnut accent that passes and flatters wood-grain shelving.

designDirections.name: Dressing Room
designDirections.bestFor: Designers selling lit dressing rooms, islands and boutique-style walk-ins in high-end homes
designDirections.headlineSample: Boutique dressing rooms and walk-in closets for {City} homes
designDirections.whyItFits: Midnight with champagne and a Didone display feel like a boutique at night, which is the feeling a top-end closet buyer is paying for.

openers.line: Your closet company has great reviews on Maps but no website, so someone in {City} dreaming about a walk-in never sees one you've built.
openers.hook: Open their Maps listing and confirm there is no Website button. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: Here's what a closet buyer would land on: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your custom closets live on Instagram, and they're lovely. But nobody can search 'pantry organization {City}' and land on your grid, and there's no way to book a measure.
openers.hook: Check the bio link and the listing. If both lead to Instagram or nothing, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: Your closets with a measure booking built in: {demo-link}

openers.line: The closet site on your listing has a free-host banner and a gallery that stops years ago. The closets on your Instagram are far better than what it shows.
openers.hook: Compare their site's newest closet with their newest post. Note the gap.
openers.linkLine: Your newest closets on a current site: {demo-link}

openers.line: On my phone your closet gallery crops every walk-in to a sliver. People plan closets on their phones, standing in the closet.
openers.hook: Only if they have a site. Load it on your phone and note what breaks. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: Your closet gallery, full-size on a phone: {demo-link}

openers.line: The only way to get a closet design from you is to call. A lot of people would rather pick a measure slot and upload the closet's dimensions at night.
openers.hook: Check for any booking or form. If none, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: A closet measure booking with room for dimensions: {demo-link}

openers.line: You've posted a few garage storage builds between the closets, and they get lost. Garage buyers are a different crowd and would book from a page of their own.
openers.hook: Count their garage posts. If there are any, name one.
openers.linkLine: A garage storage page separate from your closets: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your reviews talk about mornings that are easier now and a garage the car fits back into. That's exactly what a closet buyer wants to hear, and it sits on Maps.
openers.hook: Copy one review phrase about mornings, space or the car. Quote it back if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Those reviews next to the closets they describe: {demo-link}

openers.line: January is when everyone decides this is the year the closet gets sorted. The closet designers who appear in that search book the first quarter.
openers.hook: Use this November to January. Mention the new year in the reply.
openers.linkLine: Ready for the new-year closet rush: {demo-link}

openers.line: People measure their closet after the kids are in bed. If they can book a design consult then, they don't go looking for another closet company in the morning.
openers.hook: Call their number after hours. If voicemail only and no booking, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: A closet design booking that works at night: {demo-link}

openers.line: Saw you're hiring a closet installer. Careful installers want to see the quality of closets they'd be building before they apply.
openers.hook: Only if they posted a hiring note. Note the date.
openers.linkLine: A closet site with a careers page: {demo-link}

openers.line: You design custom closets across {City}, but no page tells someone in {Neighborhood} you'll come measure there.
openers.hook: Find towns in captions or reviews. Use the most affluent one.
openers.linkLine: A closet page for each town you cover: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your walk-ins are the hero, but a pantry or laundry system is often the second room a closet client books. A page for each would show them it's possible.
openers.hook: Look for any pantry, laundry or mudroom post. If they have one, name it.
openers.linkLine: Pantry, laundry and mudroom pages for your closet company: {demo-link}

openers.line: People letting a closet designer into their bedroom want to know who they are. A page with your designers and how the consult works removes that hesitation.
openers.hook: Check whether they ever show who designs. If not, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: Your closet designers and process on one page: {demo-link}

openers.line: Sounds like builders and agents send a lot of your closet work. Even a referred homeowner wants to browse your closets before booking a measure.
openers.hook: Look for posts tagging builders or agents. Name one if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Where a closet referral would land: {demo-link}

openers.line: The {specific recent job} you posted is the kind of closet people save to their planning boards. It should greet a buyer the moment they find you.
openers.hook: Pick their newest closet or garage and name it: room, finish and the best detail.

sequence.dm1:
Hi {Owner}, the {specific recent job} you posted is a beautiful closet.

I was looking for custom closet companies in {City} and found {Business Name}, but no site where someone can browse by room or book a design consult. I put together a sample closet and garage site, with marked placeholders where your photos would go.

Want me to send it?
sequence.dm2:
{Owner}, circling back in case this got buried. Here's the sample site for {Business Name}: {demo-link}

It has closets sorted by walk-in, reach-in, pantry and garage, a page on how the design consult works, and a measure booking that takes dimensions. If it's not for you, just say so.
sequence.call:
"Hi, is this {Owner}? I'm {Your Name}, I build websites for closet and garage storage companies here in {City}. I sent a message a couple of days ago, did you see it?"

IF NO:
"No worries. Short version: I built a sample closet site for {Business Name}, sorted by room with a garage page and a design consult booking, plus marked placeholders where your photos would go. Can I email you the link?"

IF YES:
"What did you think?"
 → let them talk, don't fill the silence
"The build runs {Build Range} depending on how many room and town pages you want, then {Care Range} a month for hosting and changes. For a closet company your size I'd quote about {Build Price}, less than one walk-in."
"Can I walk you through it for ten minutes, Tuesday or Thursday?"

CLOSE:
"I'll send a one-page scope and the deposit invoice, and we'll pick your best walk-in for the top of the page."

objections.handler: "It does, beautifully, to followers. Someone searching 'custom closets {City}' lands on Google. The site catches them and lets them book a measure."

objections.objection: The big closet franchises outspend me on ads.
objections.handler: "They do. A local designer with real closets, a named person doing the consult and town pages wins the searches they can't buy."

objections.objection: Builders give me most of my closets.
objections.handler: "Builder work is steady until starts slow. Homeowner closets and garages pay better, and the site is where they come from."

objections.objection: I'm on a lead platform already.
objections.handler: "Shared leads go to several closet companies at once and you pay either way. Your own site sends that walk-in to one designer, you."

objections.objection: I don't want to show prices.
objections.handler: "We don't need to. We show 'reach-in from' and 'walk-in from' bands in your words, or leave prices for the consult. Your call."
"{Build Range}. For you about {Build Price}: closets by room, a garage page and a design consult booking. Less than one walk-in."

{Owner}, I'm taking the {Business Name} closet demo down on Friday.

Keep it up? One word either way.
sequence.nurture:
Hi {Owner}, the new-year organising rush is a few weeks away and people are already eyeing their closets. Thought of you.

The closet site is still ready, same price. {demo-link} for another look.

bullets: Peg the build to less than one walk-in closet, never to an hourly rate.
Price the gallery by finished closets sorted by room type; the portfolio is what sells this trade.
Garage storage is a different buyer. Quote its page set as a separate line, not inside the closet build.
A design-consult booking that takes room dimensions and photos is the core. Price richer intake as its own line.
Only quote premium dressing-room pages for designers who actually build lit islands and boutique walk-ins.
Time the launch for autumn so it's found before the January organising rush.

lineItems.description: Max when the page has a sample layout, finish options and a dozen finished closets of that type.
Max with separate cabinet, slatwall and overhead pages, weight notes and a garage measure form.
Max with photo upload, wall-by-wall dimensions, a style question and calendar booking.
Max with filterable finishes, hardware and accessories on real closets.
Max when the story includes the design drawing, the finished closet and a client quote.
Max when each page has its own finished closets and a local review.

whatElseYouSell.name: Styled closet photo shoot
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A closet photographed half-empty looks like a store fixture. One styled shoot, folded sweaters and lit shelves, makes three walk-ins look like magazine pages."

whatElseYouSell.name: Instagram and Pinterest closet content plan
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Pinned pantry and walk-in ideas are where closet projects begin. Weekly posts of your own finished closets get you onto those pins with your name attached."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 3, once there are enough finished rooms.

whatElseYouSell.name: Google profile closet and garage posts
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A new walk-in or garage system on your Google profile each week, captioned by room and town."

whatElseYouSell.name: Review request a week after install
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A week after the closet goes in, once they've lived with it, the client gets a text asking for a review."

whatElseYouSell.name: New-year organising campaign
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A late-December push for 'this is the year the closet gets sorted' books January design consults before the rush."
whatElseYouSell.when: Pitch in October, run in late December.

whatElseYouSell.name: Spring garage clean-out campaign
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "When the weather turns, everyone opens the garage and sighs. A spring garage storage push catches that weekend."
whatElseYouSell.when: Pitch in February, run in March and April.

whatElseYouSell.name: Builder and realtor closet brochure
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A closet upgrade brochure builders hand new buyers, and agents leave at listings, puts your walk-ins in front of people moving."

withoutAI.whoPays: The organiser, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "Organisers sort the stuff, you build where it goes. The organiser you work with needs a site, and their clients need a closet designer."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Constant two-way referral between the person who sorts and the person who builds.

withoutAI.whoPays: The coating installer, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "A new garage floor and new garage storage go together. The coating crew needs a site with finished garages on it."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Same garage, consecutive trades, both sell on the after photo.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "Builders who use your closets need a design centre page showing upgrades, and your walk-ins sell them."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Builders earn on upgrades and the closet company becomes default.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "Designers who send you dressing rooms need portfolio sites, and your closets are some of their best rooms."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Designers buy on looks and already work with the closet company.

withoutAI.route: Movers and moving managers for downsizers
withoutAI.whoPays: The moving company, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "Movers handling downsizers know who's moving into a smaller home with less closet. They need a site, and their clients need storage."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Moves trigger closet projects; movers hear about them first.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "The supplier you buy panels and hardware from sells to installers across the region. A find-an-installer page benefits everyone."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Suppliers have budgets and their installer list is a prospect list.

withAI.pitchLine: "The organiser uploads closet photos and gets a draft sort plan and a list of storage that would help, with the closet designer to call."
withAI.whyItWorks: Organisers write those plans for every client; the tool routes builds to your client.

withAI.pitchLine: "Customers upload a garage photo and see a coated floor with wall storage before booking."
withAI.whyItWorks: A preview sells both trades in one go.

withAI.pitchLine: "Buyers in the design centre ask what closet upgrades fit their floor plan. An assistant answers from the builder's plans."
withAI.whyItWorks: Builders sell more upgrades with faster answers.

withAI.pitchLine: "The designer describes the dressing room and gets a draft spec of hanging, drawers and lighting to hand the closet company."
withAI.whyItWorks: Clear specs mean fewer revisions for both.

withAI.pitchLine: "Downsizing clients answer a few questions and get a storage plan for the new home, with a closet designer to call."
withAI.whyItWorks: Movers add value and the closet company gets warm buyers.

withAI.pitchLine: "Installers enter wall sizes and the layout, and the helper drafts a panel cut list and hardware order for the supplier."
withAI.whyItWorks: Easier ordering ties installers to one supplier.

softwareAI.name: Missed-call text-back for closet measures
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Installing a walk-in when the phone rings? The caller gets a text asking which closet or garage and a photo of the wall."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Day 30. Needs their number forwarded and two lines of wording they approve.

softwareAI.name: Closet price range builder by type and size
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Pick reach-in, walk-in, pantry or garage, enter wall lengths and a finish level, and see a range before the measure."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs their pricing by linear foot, finish and accessory.

softwareAI.name: Review replies that name the closet
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A five-star note about a new pantry gets a warm reply drafted that mentions the pull-out drawers, ready for your tap."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs ten past replies. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Deposit at design sign-off
softwareAI.pitchLine: "When the client approves the closet drawing, the deposit invoice goes out automatically and the order is released."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs their deposit rule and payment account.

softwareAI.name: Closet-photo layout preview
softwareAI.pitchLine: "The homeowner uploads a photo of their empty closet with a measurement, and sees a draft shelving and hanging layout before the consult."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs their standard modules and finished closets to check previews against. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Design-to-order tracker
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every closet from measure to drawing, approval, panel order, delivery and install on one board."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their stages and supplier lead times.

softwareAI.name: Evening design consult booking assistant
softwareAI.pitchLine: "It answers late messages, asks which room, the size and the style, and books a closet design consult."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their calendar and intake questions. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Panel cut list and hardware generator
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Approve the closet drawing and it prints the panel cut list, drawer boxes and hardware for the shop or supplier."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs their module library and panel sizes.

softwareAI.name: Client page with drawing approval
softwareAI.pitchLine: "The client sees the closet drawing, picks finishes, approves online, and sees the install date."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs the design-to-order tracker first.

softwareAI.name: Garage storage weight and layout helper
softwareAI.pitchLine: "The homeowner lists bikes, bins and tools, and it drafts a garage layout with racks and cabinets that leaves room for the cars."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs their garage products and weight ratings. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Install-day prep texts
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Two days before install, the client gets a text: empty the closet, clear the floor, and we'll take the old wire shelving."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their prep checklist.

softwareAI.name: Second-room follow-up sequence
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A few months after the walk-in, the client gets a note with a pantry or garage idea. The second closet room comes from people already happy."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs past jobs with rooms and dates.

softwareAI.name: Chatbot on closet finishes and timelines
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Questions like 'will a closet island fit in eight feet' and 'how soon can you install' get answered overnight, using your own closet rules."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs their FAQ and lead times. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Builder upgrade order portal
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Builders submit closet upgrade orders by lot and plan, and you see every one in a single list."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6, for companies with builder accounts. Needs their builder plans.

softwareAI.name: Job costing by closet type
softwareAI.pitchLine: "See whether walk-ins, pantries or garages actually pay best once panels, hardware and install hours are counted."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs supplier invoices and install hours.

softwareAI.name: Room page writer for closets
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Each month a page like 'small reach-in closet ideas', drafted from your closet notes and approved first."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs notes and approval. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Supplier lead-time and price sync
softwareAI.pitchLine: "When panel or hardware prices and lead times change, the closet range builder and install dates update."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs the supplier's sheet format.

softwareAI.name: Voice notes to closet design brief
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Talk through the client's wardrobe and wishes during the measure, and it drafts the closet design brief for the drawing."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs their brief template. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Install photo checklist
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Installers photograph level, anchors and the finished closet before leaving, so callbacks are rare and the gallery fills itself."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs their install checklist.

softwareAI.name: Installer applicant screener
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Closet installer applicants answer whether they've hung systems, read drawings and own tools, so you call only the real ones."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Any time they post a hiring note. Needs must-haves and pay. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Productise the closet range builder for independents
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: Independent closet companies, monthly per operator
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Independent closet designers all compete with franchises on the 'what does it cost' question. My range builder answers it for any of them."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Independents need tools that make them look as organised as franchises.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Installer locator for a closet component maker
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "A maker of closet panels and hardware sells through installers homeowners can't find. A locator with galleries fixes that."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Manufacturers fund dealer marketing and want installed sales.

routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: The closet franchise group, per location
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Closet franchisees need local galleries and consult booking by territory. One template, rolled out per owner."
"Organiser members need closet and garage builders to refer to. A vetted partner directory is a member benefit."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Associations want useful benefits; closet companies pay to be listed.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Agencies with closet clients rebuild galleries from scratch. License my closet template with room types and consult booking."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Agencies keep the client; you sell the finished module.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Every floor plan gets pre-drawn closet upgrades buyers can pick online, routed to one closet company."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Builders earn on upgrades and closets are an easy yes.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Move managers helping seniors downsize need closet and storage partners in every town. A shared referral board does it."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Downsizing is steady and move managers want reliable partners.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Garage makeover bundle with coating and storage partners
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: Garage coating and storage companies, per bundle
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "One garage makeover page across floor coating, storage and lighting partners, with each partner paying for their part."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Bundles sell bigger garages and split marketing cost.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Closet panel and hardware cost sheet
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Closet shops share their panel and hardware invoices and see monthly where costs are moving, built from nothing but what they sent."

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Starter kit for carpenters adding closets
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: Carpenters starting a closet line, per kit
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Carpenters adding closets need a consult script, a range sheet and a gallery page. Sell the closet kit your client runs on."

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Closet designer in the next metro
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: A closet client in a new metro
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "{City} has its closet designer. The room-by-room closet template goes to an independent one metro over."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Non-competing geography lets you reuse everything.

routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: The closet company with a stale site
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Closet sites with years-old galleries undersell the work. I move them to a current closet template in days."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Fast, visible improvement that's easy to buy.

upsellLadder.offer: Closet site build plus care plan, one contract
upsellLadder.trigger: They say yes to the demo.
upsellLadder.line: "Closet site and care plan on one contract, so a new walk-in on the gallery is a text to me."

upsellLadder.offer: Review request a week after install
upsellLadder.trigger: The first closet booked through the site is installed.
upsellLadder.line: "That pantry client has lived with it a week. Let's ask every closet client then."

upsellLadder.trigger: They install a walk-in they're proud of.
upsellLadder.line: "That walk-in deserves a styled shoot. It'll lead the closet gallery for a year."

upsellLadder.offer: Closet price range builder by type and size
upsellLadder.trigger: Sixty days of consult requests show many asking price before booking.
upsellLadder.line: "Most closet requests ask the price first. The range builder answers before the measure."

upsellLadder.trigger: Late winter, with a few garage storage jobs in the gallery.
upsellLadder.line: "Garage season is close. Let's push your garage storage before everyone opens the door and sighs."

upsellLadder.trigger: An order is delayed or they hire a second designer.
upsellLadder.line: "That late panel order was a tracking gap. Let's put every closet on one board."

upsellLadder.trigger: Several past clients ask about a pantry or garage after their walk-in.
upsellLadder.line: "Your walk-in clients keep asking about the pantry. Let's offer the second closet room to every one."
